page has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary sort-data filter-data conditional-formatting chart column-chart line-chart pie-chart chart-title cell-range >}}

## 7.1 Put the rows in order: Sort

- **Sort** puts the rows in order by one column. Each row moves as a whole.
- Click **one cell** in the table › **Data › Sort** › choose the column and
  the order.
- Quick buttons: **A→Z** (smallest first) and **Z→A** (largest first).
- The sales of the Sunrise shop in one week:

| Day | Item | Type | Qty | Total (JD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sun | Notebook | Paper | 12 | 24 |
| Sun | Juice | Drinks | 20 | 10 |
| Mon | Pen | Paper | 40 | 20 |
| Mon | Water | Drinks | 30 | 15 |
| Tue | Bag | Bags | 3 | 36 |
| Tue | Juice | Drinks | 24 | 12 |
| Wed | Notebook | Paper | 8 | 16 |
| Wed | Bag | Bags | 2 | 24 |
| Thu | Water | Drinks | 26 | 13 |
| Thu | Pen | Paper | 30 | 15 |

- Sorted by Total, largest first: the bag of Tuesday (36 JD) is on top.

![Sort by Total.](images/sort.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/table-lab.html" poster="sims/table-lab.png" title="Table Lab: sort, filter and colour the Sunrise sales" height="680" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not select only one column to sort: the other columns stay, and the
table is wrong.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Sort the week"}
Type the 10 sales of the table into `sales.xlsx`. Sort by Total, largest
first. Then sort by Day, A to Z: what is strange about the order?

::: {.check}
By Total, largest first: the bag of Tuesday (36 JD) is on top, and the
juice of Sunday (10 JD) is at the bottom. By Day, A to Z, the order is Mon,
Sun, Thu, Tue, Wed: Excel sorts the days as words, by their letters.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Sort"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Data › Filter|the colour"}
Where do you find Sort?
:   Data › Sort

    Why: Sort is on the Data tab.

Which button puts the largest total on top?
:   Z→A

    Why: Z→A sorts from the largest to the smallest.

What happens to each row when you sort?
:   it moves as a whole

    Why: Sort keeps each row together, so the table stays right.

Which sale is on top after the sort, largest first?
:   the bag of Tuesday, 36 JD

    Why: 36 JD is the biggest total in the table.
:::
:::

## 7.2 Show only some rows: Filter

- A **filter** shows only the rows you choose. The others are **hidden, not
  deleted**.
- Click one cell › **Data › Filter**. Arrows appear in the headings.
- Arrow of *Type* › tick only **Drinks** › OK: 4 rows.
- Select the totals: the status bar shows **Sum: 50**.
- **Clear Filter** shows all rows again.

![Filter the drinks.](images/filter.png){width=100%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Never delete rows to "hide" them. Use a filter.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Filter the types"}
In `sales.xlsx`, filter the Type to Paper. Select the totals: what does the
status bar show? Then clear the filter.

::: {.check}
Paper has 4 rows: 24, 20, 16 and 15 JD. The status bar shows Sum: 75.
After Clear Filter, all 10 rows come back.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Filter"}
Use the sales table of section 7.1. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="they are deleted|10"}
What happens to the rows a filter does not show?
:   they are hidden

    Why: A filter hides rows; it never deletes them.

How many rows are Drinks?
:   4

    Why: Juice on Sunday and Tuesday, and Water on Monday and Thursday.

What is the sum of the Drinks totals?
:   50 JD

    Why: 10 + 15 + 12 + 13 = 50 JD.

How do you see all rows again?
:   Clear Filter

    Why: Clear Filter shows all the rows again.
:::
:::

## 7.3 Colour by a rule: conditional formatting

- **Conditional formatting** colours cells by a rule, by itself.
- Select the totals › **Home › Conditional Formatting › Highlight Cells
  Rules › Greater Than** › 20 › a colour.
- Three cells turn green: 24, 36 and 24. The 20 stays white.
- When a number changes, the colour changes too. Remove with **Clear
  Rules**.

![A rule colours the cells.](images/cond-format.png){width=100%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Colours you add by hand do not change when the numbers change.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · The big sales"}
In `sales.xlsx`, make the rule Greater Than 20 for the totals. Add Data
Bars to the Qty column. Which item sold the most pieces?

::: {.check}
Three totals turn green: 24, 36 and 24; the 20 stays white. The longest
data bar is in the pens of Monday: 40 pieces.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Rules"}
Use the sales table of section 7.1. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Data › Sort|2"}
Where is conditional formatting?
:   Home › Conditional Formatting

    Why: Conditional formatting is on the Home tab.

How many totals are greater than 20?
:   3

    Why: 24, 36 and 24 are greater than 20.

Is the total 20 coloured by the rule Greater Than 20?
:   no

    Why: 20 is not greater than 20.

Juice changes from 12 to 22. What happens?
:   it turns green by itself

    Why: The rule checks the cells again when a number changes.
:::
:::

## 7.4 Show it as a picture: charts

- **Column chart:** compare amounts. **Line chart:** a change over time.
  **Pie chart:** the parts of one whole.
- Select a small table › **Insert › Recommended Charts** (or Column, Line,
  Pie).
- Click **Chart Title** and write what the chart shows.
- The **+** next to the chart adds data labels.

![The right chart for the question.](images/chart-types.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/chart-lab.html" poster="sims/chart-lab.png" title="Chart Lab: the right chart for the question" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"Chart Title" is not a title. Write what the chart shows.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Two charts"}
Make the table *Type / Sales* (Paper 75, Drinks 50, Bags 60). Make a column
chart with a real title, and a pie chart with data labels.

::: {.check}
A column chart with three columns (Paper 75, Drinks 50, Bags 60) and a
real title, for example "Sales by type in one week (JD)". The pie chart
shows the three parts of 185 JD, each with its label.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Charts"}
Choose the right chart. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="a table|a picture"}
Compare Paper, Drinks and Bags?
:   a column chart

    Why: Columns compare amounts side by side.

The sales from Sunday to Thursday?
:   a line chart

    Why: A line shows a change over time.

The part of each type in the 185 JD?
:   a pie chart

    Why: A pie shows the parts of one whole.

The sales of five shops in one month?
:   a column chart

    Why: Five shops are amounts to compare.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Rana's Questions {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Huda asks Rana six questions about the sales of the week: the biggest sale,
only the drinks, big totals in green, the change over the days, the three
types compared, and the part of each type in **185 JD**.

{{< sim file="sims/ranas-questions.html" poster="sims/ranas-questions.png" title="Rana's Questions: the right Excel tool" kind="game" height="520" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Rana's answers (harder)"}
The sales of the week are in the table of section 7.1: Paper, Drinks and
Bags, 185 JD in all. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="type the numbers again|delete the other rows|45 JD"}
Which sale was the biggest? Which tool shows it fast?
:   Sort by Total, largest first

    Why: Sort puts the biggest total on top.

"Show me only the drinks." Which tool?
:   Filter the column Type

    Why: A filter shows only the rows of one type.

"Make every total above 20 JD green, also next week." Which tool?
:   Conditional formatting

    Why: A rule colours the totals by itself, also next week.

What is the total of the Paper sales?
:   75 JD

    Why: 24 + 20 + 16 + 15 = 75 JD.

On which day were the sales highest?
:   Tuesday, 48 JD

    Why: Tuesday: 36 + 12 = 48 JD, more than any other day.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Sort puts the rows in order; click one cell first.
- A filter shows only some rows; it never deletes them.
- Conditional formatting colours cells by a rule, also when numbers change.
- Column: compare. Line: change over time. Pie: parts of a whole. Always a
  real title.
